scenario: AITA for getting mad at my bf for always walking in front of me? | Everytime my boyfriend and I are walking somewhere, he tends to walk much faster than me. I’m actually a pretty fast walker myself when alone, but when going out with him, either I’m in heels half the time so it’s harder to walk super fast, or even in flats, sometimes I just want to walk alongside him and hold hands and have a conversation. It’s hard to hear him or I’m struggling to keep up. I’ve brought it up to him multiple times but he says he just has longer strides (he’s maybe 6” taller than me) and can’t help it. We just went on vacation and walking around a new city, it was the same thing and I finally blew up at him saying that I don’t feel like his girlfriend when he won’t ever walk beside me. AITA and he really can’t help it?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for my boyfriend to always walk faster than me, especially when we're out together. I've mentioned this to him before, and he says it's just because he has longer strides because he's taller. But every time we go somewhere, I end up struggling to keep up, especially if I'm wearing heels or flats. I just want to walk alongside him, hold hands, and have a conversation. It's hard to hear him or keep up when he's walking so fast. We went on vacation recently, and it was the same thing. I finally blew up at him, saying I don't feel like his girlfriend when he won't ever walk beside me. Now I'm wondering if I'm overreacting or if he really can't help it. Is it wrong for him to keep walking faster, or is it just a matter of his stride? I guess I need to think about why this bothers me so much. It's not just about keeping up physically; it's also about feeling connected and valued in the relationship. When he's walking ahead, I feel like he's not considering my pace or my desire to be close to him. It makes me feel like he's not prioritizing our time together or my comfort. On the other hand, he says he can't help it because of his height and longer strides. Maybe he doesn't realize how much it affects me. I wonder if there's a way we can compromise or adjust our walking pace so that we can both be comfortable. Maybe he could slow down a bit, or I could try to adjust my stride to match his. I also think about how communication plays a role here. I've brought it up before, but maybe I need to approach the conversation differently. Instead of getting upset, I could explain how it makes me feel and ask if we can find a solution together. That way, it's not about blaming him but working on the issue as a team. Another thing to consider is whether this is a bigger issue in our relationship. If small things like this are causing frequent arguments, it might be a sign that we need to work on our communication and problem-solving skills in general. It's important to address these issues before they lead to bigger problems. I also wonder if there's a deeper reason why this bothers me so much. Maybe it's about feeling neglected or unimportant in the relationship. If he's consistently not considering my needs in something as simple as walking together, it could indicate a pattern in how he treats me in other areas. In the end, I think it's important to address this issue in a constructive way. Instead of getting angry, I should express my feelings calmly and see if we can find a middle ground. It's possible that he doesn't realize the impact of his walking pace on me, and with open communication, we can find a solution that works for both of us.
